reader.requirement: In the Report Section PAGE-COUNTER may be referenced only in a SOURCE clause (as a SUM operand, CONTROL operand, TYPE CF operand, RESET operand or subscript it is refused), while in the Procedure Division it is accepted in every context that admits an integer data item, sending or receiving.
reader.edition-search: grep DialectLevel/CobolVersion/ConstructRegistry in ReportSectionNameIn, ScreenReportSubscripts, ReportWriterBinder.CounterExpr/CounterPlace and ExpressionBinder lines 840-880 and 1025: none on the counter path.

reader.notes: Every non-SOURCE Report Section use is refused and every Procedure Division integer context works. Outside this verdict: four of the refusals (CONTROL, TYPE CF, RESET, SUM operand) carry COBOL0899, the catalog's NotImplemented code, for genuine rule violations at every edition (same at --std 2023), and none names this rule.
reader.at-2023: pc_rs_control at --std 2023: the same COBOL0899 refusal

refuter.evidence: I checked the reader's subscript refusal (SOURCE TE(PAGE-COUNTER) inside a SOURCE clause, COBOL2751, which cites only §2023) against the 1985 text. 1985 has its own rule: 'OK  §1985:XIII.1.2.4  (1.2.4 Subscripting)  the text is in the clause' ('neither a sum counter nor the special registers LINE-COUNTER and PAGE-COUNTER can be used as a subscript'), so the refusal is right at 85. Outside the Report Section and the Procedure Division (§1985:XIII.1.2.2: 'may be referenced only in the SOURCE clause of the Report Section and in Procedure Division statements'), pc_ws_odo and pc_ws_odo_q (WS OCCURS DEPENDING ON PAGE-COUNTER [OF R-A]) are refused with COBOL2024. A 2002 SOURCE form, SOURCE PAGE-COUNTER + 1, is refused at 85 with COBOL0900. Procedure Division integer contexts the reader did not run, from pc_more_contexts: SET PAGE-COUNTER TO IX gives 3, and SET IX TO PAGE-COUNTER then TE(IX) gives C; STRING ... POINTER PAGE-COUNTER gives 5; UNSTRING COUNT IN gives 2 and TALLYING IN gives 2; SEARCH VARYING PAGE-COUNTER gives 4; EVALUATE gives 4. SET PAGE-COUNTER TO 5 is refused (COBOL2326), as §1985:VI.6.23.4 GR5 Table 1 requires: an integer literal to an integer data item is 'No/3c' ('OK  §1985:VI.6.23.3 SR2', 'OK  §1985:VI.6.23.4 GR5'). cite.py: 'OK  §1985:XIII.3.5.5 SR2 ...'; 'OK  §1985:XIII.1.2.2 ...'.
